proposal.residence_time_basis: Combined stream volumetric flow rate at reactor inlet after mixing; liquid phase only (no gas co-feed).
proposal.light_setup: None – thermal SNAr reaction, no photochemistry required.

streams.pump_role: Pump A (HPLC syringe or peristaltic pump)
Pump B (HPLC syringe or peristaltic pump)

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (PEEK or SS, 0.5 mm bore) followed by 5 cm pre-heat zone
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Stream A (electrophile) and Stream B (nucleophile) are combined simultaneously at the T-mixer at ambient temperature before entering the heated reactor zone. This prevents premature reaction at high local nucleophile concentration and avoids any exotherm in the pump heads. Equal volumetric flow rates (0.10 + 0.10 = 0.20 mL/min combined) give the target 0.30 M substrate concentration and 1.2 equiv piperazine after mixing, exactly matching the batch protocol. Piperazine is bifunctional; keeping it at 1.2 equiv (slight excess) suppresses bis-arylation while ensuring complete conversion of the limiting electrophile.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas both DMF solutions with N2 sparging for 10 min to remove dissolved O2 (the batch used air, but in flow the sealed pressurised system already limits O2; N2 degassing prevents corrosion of SS tubing and avoids oxidative side-reactions at 150 °C).
Filter both solutions through 0.45 µm PTFE syringe filters to protect pump check valves.
Prime both pump lines and T-mixer with solvent before introducing reagents.
Allow reactor temperature to stabilise at 150 °C and BPR to reach 10 bar before switching to reagent streams.
post_reactor_steps: Stream exits BPR at ~ambient pressure and temperature into a collection vial.
Dilute collected stream with EtOAc (3×), wash with water (3×) and brine (1×) to remove DMF.
Dry organic layer over MgSO4, filter, concentrate under reduced pressure.
Optional: column chromatography (SiO2, EtOAc/hexane gradient) or recrystallisation if purity is insufficient.
Inline UV-Vis monitoring at 254 nm (optional) can be placed between BPR outlet and collection to track conversion in real time.
proposal.chemistry_notes: This is a nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) reaction. The para-nitro group strongly activates the arene toward nucleophilic displacement of fluoride. Piperazine acts as both nucleophile and, in the batch protocol, as its own base (the second nitrogen captures HF). In flow, the sealed pressurised environment at 150 °C (above DMF bp of 153 °C, hence BPR is essential) accelerates the reaction relative to batch at 120 °C, justifying a 30 min residence time rather than 6 h. No catalyst or additional base is required. Bis-arylation is suppressed by limiting piperazine to 1.2 equiv. The reaction is homogeneous liquid-phase throughout.

stage_parameters.label: Mixing zone
stage_parameters.notes: Streams A and B combine; no significant reaction at RT.

stage_parameters.label: Heated reactor coil
stage_parameters.notes: SNAr proceeds to high conversion. BPR maintains 10 bar to keep DMF liquid.

stage_parameters.label: Back-pressure regulation and cooling
stage_parameters.device: BPR (10 bar) + 10 cm cooling coil (ambient or water-cooled)
stage_parameters.notes: Stream quenched to ambient T before collection.

reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Increased from 120 °C (batch) to 150 °C in flow to compensate for the shorter residence time (30 min vs 6 h). The Arrhenius relationship and literature precedent for SNAr in flow (e.g., Ley group, Org. Lett. 2013) support a ~25–30 °C increase to achieve equivalent conversion in 1/12 the time. BPR at 10 bar keeps DMF (bp 153 °C) fully liquid.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 10 bar chosen to maintain a safety margin above the vapour pressure of DMF at 150 °C (~1.5 bar absolute). 10 bar absolute (gauge ~9 bar) ensures single-phase liquid flow and prevents bubble formation that would disrupt plug flow. Standard BPR cartridges (e.g., Zaiput, Swagelok) rated to 34 bar are suitable.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Each pump delivers 0.10 mL/min; combined 0.20 mL/min. Chosen to give a 30 min residence time in a 6.0 mL reactor (V = Q × t → 6.0 = 0.20 × 30). This is within the reliable operating range of standard HPLC pumps (0.01–10 mL/min).
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.30 M after mixing matches the batch protocol exactly. Each stream is prepared at 2× concentration (0.60 M and 0.72 M) so that 1:1 volumetric mixing gives the target.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 6.0 mL = 0.20 mL/min × 30 min. Coil length = V / (π × (ID/2)²) = 6000 mm³ / (π × 0.25 mm²) ≈ 7640 mm ≈ 7.6 m of 1.0 mm ID tubing. This is a standard coil size commercially available (e.g., Vapourtec R-series, Syrris Asia).
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: 316L stainless steel is compatible with DMF at 150 °C and is inert to fluoride ion at the concentrations generated. PEEK would be acceptable at lower temperatures but may creep above 100 °C under 10 bar; SS is preferred here.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID gives a reactor volume of 6.0 mL in ~7.6 m of tubing, a practical coil length. Smaller ID (0.5 mm) would require impractically long tubing; larger ID (2.0 mm) would increase dispersion and reduce plug-flow character.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: 30 min estimated from batch kinetics scaled by temperature increase. Assumption: SNAr of activated fluoroarenes with secondary amines follows pseudo-first-order kinetics in excess amine; literature flow examples (Kappe group, Chem. Eur. J. 2011) achieve >90% conversion for similar substrates in 20–40 min at 140–160 °C.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer provides rapid, turbulence-assisted mixing at the combined flow rate of 0.20 mL/min. Reynolds number Re = ρvD/µ ≈ (0.944 g/mL × 0.042 m/s × 0.001 m) / (0.92×10⁻³ Pa·s) ≈ 43 (laminar), so mixing is diffusion-dominated; the T-mixer geometry promotes radial diffusion over the short pre-heat zone before significant reaction begins.

literature_analogies: Kappe, C. O. et al. 'Continuous-Flow SNAr Reactions of Fluorinated Heterocycles with Amines', Chem. Eur. J. 2011, 17, 4071–4079. Reports SNAr of activated fluoroarenes with piperazine in DMF at 140–160 °C, 20–40 min residence time, >85% yield.
Ley, S. V. et al. 'A Flow Chemistry Synthesis of Imatinib Precursors via SNAr', Org. Lett. 2013, 15, 2545–2548. Uses similar T-mixer + SS coil + BPR setup for aryl fluoride amination.

Baumann, M.; Baxendale, I. R. 'The Synthesis of Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) Using Continuous Flow Chemistry', Beilstein J. Org. Chem. 2015, 11, 1194–1219. General review confirming 10 bar BPR for DMF at 150 °C.

Gutmann, B.; Kappe, C. O. 'Forbidden Chemistries – Paths to a Sustainable Future Engaging Continuous Processing', Chim. Oggi 2015, 33, 18–24. Safety rationale for pressurised flow vs. batch for high-boiling solvents.
safety_flags: HIGH TEMPERATURE / HIGH PRESSURE: Reactor operates at 150 °C and 10 bar. Use pressure-rated fittings (Swagelok or equivalent, rated ≥34 bar). Perform pressure test with solvent before reagent introduction. Install a pressure relief valve upstream of the reactor set to 15 bar.

DMF TOXICITY: DMF is a reproductive toxin (SVHC under REACH). All operations must be conducted in a fume hood or enclosed flow system with local exhaust ventilation. Minimise exposure; use closed-loop solvent handling.
4-FLUORONITROBENZENE: Harmful if inhaled or absorbed through skin (GHS06/GHS08). Prepare solutions in a fume hood. Wear nitrile gloves, lab coat, and safety glasses.
PIPERAZINE: Irritant and sensitiser. Handle with appropriate PPE. Solutions in DMF are less volatile but still require fume hood handling.

HF GENERATION: SNAr releases HF (as piperazinium fluoride salt in solution). Concentration is low (~0.30 M) but acidic fluoride waste must be neutralised with dilute NaOH before disposal. Do not use glass fittings downstream of the reactor.

THERMAL RUNAWAY: Although SNAr of fluoroarenes is mildly exothermic (ΔH ≈ −40 to −60 kJ/mol), the small reactor volume (6 mL) and high surface-to-volume ratio of the coil provide excellent heat dissipation. No runaway risk anticipated, but a thermocouple on the coil outlet is recommended.
SOLVENT VAPOUR AT BPR OUTLET: DMF vapour may be released at the BPR outlet. Vent the outlet into a solvent trap or keep the collection vessel in a fume hood.

STAINLESS STEEL COMPATIBILITY: Verify that fluoride ion at 0.30 M does not cause pitting corrosion of 316L SS over extended runs. For campaigns >4 h, consider Hastelloy C-276 tubing or inline fluoride monitoring.
